text:
Predicates:
EatsSalad(x) ::: x eats salads regularly.
HealthConsciousHome(x) ::: x grew up in a health-conscious childhood home.
Nutritional(x) ::: x fulfills their nutritional daily intakes.
GoodRelationship(x) ::: x has good relationships with their parents.
VisitsGym(x) ::: x visits the gym at least once a day.
Taylor ::: the individual named Taylor.
Premises:
∀x (EatsSalad(x) → VeryConscious(x)) ::: All people who eat salads regularly are very conscious about their health and eating habits.
∀x (HealthConsciousHome(x) → EatsSalad(x)) ::: All people who grew up in health-conscious childhood homes eat salads regularly.
∀x (Nutritional(x) → HealthConsciousHome(x)) ::: All people who fulfill nutritional daily intakes grew up in health-conscious childhood homes.
∀x (GoodRelationship(x) → Nutritional(x)) ::: If people have good relationships with their parents, then they fulfill their nutritional daily intakes.
∀x (GoodRelationship(x) → ¬EatsSalad(x)) ::: If people have good relationships with their parents, then they do not eat salads regularly.
∀x (VisitsGym(x) → Nutritional(x)) ::: If people visit the gym at least once a day, then they always fulfill their daily nutritional intakes.
(TaylorGrewUpInHealthyHome ∧ TaylorGoodRelationship) ∨ ¬(TaylorGrewUpInHealthyHome ∨ TaylorGoodRelationship) ::: It is either both true that Taylor grew up in a health-conscious childhood home and she has a good relationship with her parents, or it is true that Taylor neither grew up in a health-conscious childhood home nor has a good relationship with her parents.
Conclusion:
¬TaylorGrewUpInHealthyHome ∧ ¬VisitsGym(Taylor) ::: Taylor neither grew up in a health-conscious childhood home nor does she visit the gym at least once a day.
